chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Yaqubi, from Musa ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Muyassar, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the deceased dies at the beginning of the day, he does not spend the afternoon (or night) except in his grave.'

key_terms.أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ: at the beginning of the day
key_terms.يَقِيلُ: to spend the afternoon or night (specifically the time after midday until nightfall)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on delaying burial if death occurs early in the day?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia emphasis on prompt burial (tasri') to prevent the body from remaining exposed or unburied overnight, reflecting the practical urgency of honoring the deceased. The phrase 'la yaqilu' specifically denotes spending the afternoon and night, highlighting the distinction between same-day burial and delayed interment. This ruling aligns with the broader jurisprudential principle that haste in burial is preferred unless specific circumstances, such as waiting for close relatives or preparing the grave, necessitate a brief delay.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Al Yaqouby, from Musa Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Muyassar, from Haroun Bin Al Jahm, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the dying one dies at the beginning of the day, he should not snooze except in his grave’ (spend night in the grave – so should be buried during the day).
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-‘ Abbas ibn Ma’ruf from al-Ya‘qubiy from Musa ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Muyassir from Harun ibn al-Jahm from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
if one dies in the beginning of the day, he cannot have a nap anywhere other than his grave.”
